title: docs(automation): three declaration-truth residues on the run-history row — a one-way discriminator, the row's step log, and the write that names its reader
body:
Fixes #15336

Authored in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01ToDPcx9AESFubJkDiFMtKW` (⚠️ in prose, deliberately: measured on this PR, a REST **edit** to a body APPENDS the bare footer block while the session-URL footer I sent on **create** survived verbatim — so carrying the session-URL form through an edit leaves two footers. Durable attribution therefore lives here, and the tail footer below is the platform's).

⛔ **Three of the card's six items, deliberately — not all six. This is a partial delivery and says so, because taking a partial delivery for a complete one is this card's own defect species.**

| item | subject | here? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | the 50-entry store-less journal cap bounds restorability | ⛔ **no** — a product question the card itself names as one: 「Whether a store-less deployment is expected to be restorable at all is the actual question, **and it is a product one**」. It also lives in `engine.ts`, held by another in-flight PR |
| 2 | restore → resume → crash re-arms on the next boot | ⛔ **no** — already ruled |
| 3 | the two-witness read cannot cover another replica's failed history write | ⛔ **no** — already ruled, same condition as 2 |
| 4 | `variables_json`'s `⇔` is over-strong in the `⇐` direction | ✅ yes |
| 5 | the `#13909` docblock claims the row's steps are "AS OF THE PAUSE" | ✅ yes |
| 6 | `recordTerminal`'s JSDoc lacks a cross-reference | ✅ yes |

Items 2 and 3 are **recorded, not pending**: the maintainer's decision batch #21 point 3 rules 「**shape 2 仅在与保住 exactly-once 的持久 claim/lease 同批设计时重开** —— 单独的顺序翻转 ⛔ **不做**」. ⛔ They are not designed, not prototyped and not offered as alternatives anywhere in this diff.

⛔ **No behaviour changes.** Every shape described below is the ruled design, measured as it already is. What was wrong was the text.

## Item 4 — the falsifying shape, and how the row is known to be rewritten with NULLs

The description declared presence and "this run had a pause its resume consumed before a downstream node failed" **equivalent**. The forward direction holds. The reverse fails for one shape: **a run that stranded, was restored, and then finished.**

The mechanism is in the writer, and the producer's own contract text already states it — `RunRecord.consumedSuspension` in `engine.ts`: "Cleared by the next terminal record for the same run — a restored run that resumes to completion upserts this row without a snapshot — so 'restorable' cannot outlive the condition it describes." In the store, `recordTerminal` spreads `serializeConsumedSuspension(record.consumedSuspension, …)` into the row unconditionally, and that helper's no-snapshot arm returns an `empty` object of five explicit `null`s — with the reason written beside it: "ALWAYS all four keys, `null` when there is no snapshot: this is an UPSERT, and a restored run that later finishes must CLEAR what it carried."

⇒ the same `run_`-prefixed row is rewritten with NULLs, so **absence does not imply "never had one"**. The runtime already refuses to read that direction: `restoreConsumedSuspension`'s last refusal is annotated "⛔ Deliberately does not claim WHICH: 'it never paused' and 'its snapshot is gone' are indistinguishable from here" — which is this direction being unavailable, honestly. ⇒ a truth fix, not a behaviour fix.

## Item 5 — the durable row keeps the failed step; only the journal copy does not

`deserializeConsumedSuspension`'s docblock called the rebuilt snapshot's `steps` the log "AS OF THE PAUSE", with the parenthetical "(the engine trims the failed attempt's steps off the snapshot before recording)". Both halves are true of the **journal copy only**:

- the journal copy is built by `journalConsumedSuspension` as `{ ...run, steps: run.steps.slice(0, stepCountAtPause), … }` — trimmed, in-process, and never persisted;
- the row's `steps_json` is written by `recordTerminal` as `serializeStepsBounded(record.steps)`, and `record.steps` is `compactStepsForHistory(entry.steps)` — `recordLog`'s log of the **whole** run. `engine.ts` says so at the resume site: the summary "covers the WHOLE run — the steps before the pause and after it are one log";
- **both** bounds on that column keep the failure on purpose: `compactStepLogForHistory` selects "Every **failure**, wherever it occurred — the reason the run is worth keeping", and `serializeStepsBounded` halves the tail until it fits, i.e. **trims the head** ("the newest steps carry the failure").

⇒ a snapshot rebuilt from a row carries steps the pause never had. `steps` is the one field of the rebuild that does not come from the snapshot columns.

## Item 6 — the cross-reference, plus one stale phrase in the same docblock

`recordTerminal` now names the verb that reads what it writes (`AutomationEngine.restoreConsumedSuspension`, through `loadTerminal` and `deserializeConsumedSuspension`) and the three properties of this write that are that verb's inputs rather than local detail.

⚠️ **One bounded in-place correction, disclosed rather than left behind:** the same docblock's first line said "Persist a TERMINAL run (completed / failed)". The terminal vocabulary has had **four** members since #15223 removed that exact two-member fold from both ends of this write — `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` is `completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out`, `RunRecord.status` is `TerminalRunStatus`, and this file's own `isTerminalStatus` delegates to the one vocabulary. Leaving a false statement in a docblock being rewritten for truth, in a PR about declaration truth, was the worse option. Same defect class, same file, one phrase, no new verification surface.

## What is pinned, what is not, and the direction observed

Two of the three have an executable surface; **item 6 does not** — a cross-reference in prose cannot be pinned without writing a test that restates the comment, so ⛔ none was written.

New pins in `suspended-run-store.test.ts` (3 tests, in the file that already owns this store's doubles — no new fake engine, no new ledger entry):

1. the strand writes the snapshot, and the restored run's completion **clears all five columns** — with the snapshot's presence asserted first as the positive control;
2. ⭐ the **indistinguishability itself**: the restored-then-finished row compares **equal** to the row of a run that never paused, across every column the discriminator is read from — with a firing control in the same test (the same comparison **separates** them while the snapshot is still on the row);
3. the row-rebuilt snapshot's `steps` equal the **whole run's** log and not the pause's — with the four snapshot-sourced fields asserted as the positive control that the rebuild is real.

**RED before GREEN, by state.** Both ablations mutate committed state, prove the mutation on disk, run, and restore by state. Resolution path: the test imports `./suspended-run-store.js` relative, which vitest resolves to the package's own `src/*.ts` — no `dist/` leg, so no build sits between the mutation and the run, and the RED itself proves the mutation reached the running test.

| leg | mutation | on-disk proof | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A | `if (!run) return empty;` → `return {};` (stop writing the NULLs) | blob `15c7f381` → `ffa26a83`; injected text 1 occurrence, removed text 0 | 🔴 **2 failed, 1 passed** — pins 1 and 2 red, pin 3 correctly unaffected |
| B | `serializeStepsBounded(record.steps)` → `serializeStepsBounded(record.consumedSuspension?.steps ?? record.steps)` (make the row's steps be as of the pause — i.e. the world the old docblock described) | blob `15c7f381` → `59ce607e`; injected 1, removed 0 | 🔴 **1 failed, 2 passed** — pin 3 red, pins 1 and 2 correctly unaffected |

Restore after each leg, by state and not by exit code: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty, `git hash-object` back to `15c7f381` = the `HEAD` blob, occurrence counts back to 1/0. Each leg ran under a `trap` on EXIT INT TERM that restores with an absolute path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, restoring with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` (⛔ never a bare `git checkout --`), and refused to start unless the tree already matched the `HEAD` blob.

🟢 GREEN at the merged head: package suite **129 files / 1542 tests passed**, `typecheck` exit 0 — and the new test file is in **both** tsc programs (`tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`, 1 `--listFiles` hit each), so that typecheck really covers it.

## What else projects from the `variables_json` description — measured, each zero with a firing control

The seat's pre-measured obligation verified independently: `variables_json` at `platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts` belongs to **`sys_email_template`** (neighbours `locale` / `subject` / `body_html` / `from_address` / `reply_to`), and the platform checklist's one `variables_json` row names `sys_email_template` too. ⇒ no translation regeneration obliged. Then the rest of the generators:

| projection | reading | firing control |
|:--|:--|:--|
| i18n bundles | **0** — the projection is declared per package by `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts`, and there are exactly **9** in the tree (platform-objects, 5 plugins, service-messaging / service-realtime / service-storage). `service-automation` has none, and no `*.generated.ts` in the repo contains `sys_automation_run` | `sys_email_template` hits 7 generated bundle files on the same grep; the 9-config roster is a positive list, not a failed grep |
| `scripts/adr-anchors/` | **0** files name either source file | the same grep over the same directory returns 1 for `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`, which is anchored |
| `docs/qa/platform-checklist/` | **0** rows quote this description or the `⇔` claim | 18 files mention automation; the `sys_automation_run` rows are about retention and paused-row persistence |
| `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` | records `{name, file, reach, tenantField, reasons}` for this object — **no description** | the entry is printed in full, so this is a read of the record, not of its absence |
| `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json` | ⭐ **a real projection**: the cross-package prose-id leg counts internal ids in this file's *prose* and pins `#2585: 1 · #3801: 1 · #7533: 2`. Shrink-only **and** stale-detecting, so it reds in both directions | `pnpm check:doc-authoring` exit 0 ⇒ my edit moved neither count. The new clause carries no issue id, by construction |
| hand-written docs | `scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs`: **0 docs** name either anchor (`ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore`, `SysAutomationRun`) | `AutomationEngine` → 8 files, `ObjectKernel` → 25 on the same corpus grep. ⚠️ One corpus hit exists and is a **named false positive**: `docs/audits/2026-09-tenancy-ledger-namespace-regexp-census.md:184` names `ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore` — in a tenancy/organization-stamping row, a process record outside the corpus, and nothing in this diff touches organization resolution |
| `packages/spec/liveness/**` (the liveness ledger, 36 files) | **0** name this column, this object or either source file. ⭐ The one hit is `email_template.json`, whose evidence line is plugin-email's `variables_json` — the **third** independent place that same collision appears (translation bundle, platform checklist, liveness ledger), all `sys_email_template` | `maxLength` hits 2 of the 36 on the identical grep; an entry's shape (`type` / `_note` / `props`) is printed, so the zero is a read of the record |
| `check:i18n-coverage` · `check:i18n` | both exit **0**, run directly rather than inferred: coverage reports `13 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new`; the bundle gate reports `9 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys` and prints its own population, in which the three services are messaging / realtime / storage | ⭐ the gate printing its own roster is the control: `service-automation` is absent from the declared population, so this is a positive list reading and not a failed grep |
| published bytes | the description reaches `dist/index.js` + `dist/index.cjs`; `recordTerminal`'s docblock reaches `dist/index.d.ts` + `.d.cts`; the module-private docblock reaches **nothing** | a pre-existing description hits the same two files (positive), the module-private docblock 0 (negative), `recordTerminal` present in dist (the negative control's grep fires) |

⇒ published bytes move, so this takes a **`patch` changeset** and ⛔ not `skip-changeset`.

Clause-②: no

Both limbs measured on the diff rather than asserted. **Limb A — does it widen the accept set?** No. In the two shipped source files the *only* non-comment added line is the `description:` string value; there is no schema, parser, validator or accept set anywhere in the diff, and a field description is documentation on an existing key, not a member of any accept set. The caveat was taken seriously — a shipped object description **is** metadata, and it does ship (`dist/index.js`) — which is what the changeset pays for; it is still not an accept set, and the projection table above is the search for any schema projection that would make it one. **Limb B — a new exported symbol, or a new key on a published payload?** Neither: **0** added lines containing `export` across the whole diff (control: 284 added lines, so the grep fires), and no key is added anywhere — the one key whose *value* changed already existed. ⚠️ `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no` answers **NOT MEASURED on all 4 files** ("no declared surface covers it"), so the mechanical half gives no verdict in either direction here and this declaration rests on the hand measurement above.

## Gates

Derived from the actual diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, re-derived on the merged head (**identical 60-command set**, change set still exactly these 4 paths, three-dot semantics), run, and reconciled with `--ran`: **60 derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, every command recorded as `command :: exit code` so the zero is derived rather than claimed. All 60 exit **0**.

⭐ One of them first answered **exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET**, and was **not** rounded up: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` reads built output and named 49 packages with no `dist/`. Its CI host is ci.yml's `Build Core`, which runs `pnpm build` first — so the prerequisite was satisfied the same way (`pnpm build`, 73/73 tasks) and the gate **re-run to a real 0**: "104 published require entry point(s) across 67 package(s) load; 603 emitted CommonJS file(s) parse". Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (slot `dev-15336`); its own verdict lines: `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 423s` (build), `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 7s` (tests).

Outside the derived 60, and stated rather than implied: the 47 artifact-roster families, the 11 declared-wide populations, the 5 path-scheduled CI jobs and the workflow-valued commands are CI's, printed by the tool under their own headings — ⛔ their silence here is not a clearance.

## Docs Drift Check — answered, including the read it says it can never do

The bot reports 「**nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**」. The full answer is a comment on this PR; in summary, and on the tree the bot named (`5bff82ff5e41ed4d7c0ff67442a7da3932daae8b`, the merge of head `db6c1b503` into base `9540590ba`, fetched as the PR merge ref and confirmed by sha equality — ⛔ not a worktree cut from an older `main`):

- its `--json` rows reproduce exactly (`docs: []`, the same 2 anchors, every other list empty), from a comparison worktree whose `git status --porcelain` is **0 entries** — which repairs the bot's own ⚠️ caveat that its checkout 「carried **uncommitted changes**」;
- the **emitter-blind hand read** was done by concept vocabulary rather than by identifier, one command shape for subjects and controls alike, with controls firing at `stranded` 6 · `re-arm` 8 · `suspend` 15 · `consumed` 29 · `snapshot` 54 · `pause` 24. **No page restates item 4's `⇐` direction** (`never paused` / `never suspended` / `had a pause` / `did not pause` all **0**) and **none carries item 5's over-claim** (`as of the pause` / `at suspend time` / `steps so far` / `before the pause` all **0**). ⭐ The one page that states item 5's rule by its inputs states it in the **corrected** direction, which is evidence the docblock was the outlier;
- three named false positives rather than a bare "not falsified": `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (a word collision with package versions), `sys_metadata_history` under "history row", and a TTL tombstone example under "terminal row";
- the coarse 6-page `packageMentionDocs` fallback row is answered page by page too.
